title: Token-share rebalancer: KV-aware soft-preemption and slot consolidation for continuous batching
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Problem summary: Our continuous batching pipeline currently uses hard preemption and simple priority bands to enforce SLOs. This causes suboptimal fairness across tenants and frequent KV cache churn that increases GPU memory fragmentation and token latency variance. Goal: implement a token-share rebalancer that uses soft-preemption, KV-cache locality signals, and slot consolidation to meet per-tenant SLOs while improving overall throughput and reducing KV eviction churn. The feature should be pluggable in the existing preemptor interface and configurable via per-queue policies in Dedicated/Hosted modes.
design_notes: Core ideas: (1) Soft-preemption: instead of immediately evicting a request, mark it as preemptible and allow it to drain its most cache-local tokens within a short grace window. (2) Token-share accounting: maintain a moving token budget per tenant and per-priority slice; rebalance slots by moving fractional token shares rather than whole-slot steals. (3) KV locality score: each request carries a kv_locality score computed from prefix hit rates and model KV slab residency; preemptor prefers evicting requests with low locality to avoid high-cost evictions. (4) Slot consolidation: periodically coalesce small partially-filled slots into compacted slots on the same GPU to reduce fragmentation and free contiguous memory for large KV slabs. (5) Backoff and fairness multiplier: tenants with repeated SLO misses receive temporary fairness multiplier boosts to avoid starvation. Implementation will extend the preemptor state machine and add a light-weight per-tenant token ledger persisted in runtime metadata.
acceptance_criteria: New soft-preempt path implemented and behind runtime flag 'token_share_rebalancer'
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating request marked preemptible drains within configured grace window (default 50ms)
KV eviction rate decreases by at least 20% on synthetic mixed-workload replay compared to baseline hard preemptor
P95 token latency for low-priority tenants does not regress more than 10% while high-priority SLOs remain met
GPU memory fragmentation metric (max contiguous free slab) improves by >=15% during consolidation runs
Documentation updated with configuration knobs and recommended defaults
Safety rollback: feature can be toggled off cluster-wide within 2 minutes and degrades gracefully
plan: Spike (2d): microbench KV-locality scoring and token-budget ledger format; benchmark eviction cost
Design PR (3d): proto API for soft-preempt signals and slot consolidation scheduler
Implementation (10d): preemptor state changes, token ledger, KV-locality hooks, unit + integration tests
Perf evaluation (4d): replay mixed tenant traces on staging GPU fleet; record KV eviction, p95 latency, fragmentation
Canary rollout (5d): enable for 10% of traffic with telemetry gating and automated rollback
Full rollout (2d): staged expansion to 100% after telemetry stability
test_plan: Unit tests for token ledger consistency under concurrent updates
Integration tests simulating interleaved KV hits and misses with eviction assertions
Stress replay: 24-hour mixed-tenant workload comparing baseline and rebalancer
Fuzzing: random preemptible flag toggles to validate no deadlocks in preemptor state machine
SLO regression suite: ensure existing SLOs for control tenants remain green
rollout: Feature rolled out behind runtime flag 'token_share_rebalancer'
Stage 0: internal infra clusters (dev/staging) - validate correctness
Stage 1: 10% canary on Hosted (non-critical customers) with telemetry gating
Stage 2: 50% with selected Dedicated customers after acceptance
Stage 3: global rollout with monitoring runbook active
